choices.text: Pollination and fertilisation are the same event with two names
Fertilisation happens first, then pollination delivers the seed
Pollination is delivery: the male gamete must still fuse with the ovule for fertilisation.
A flower is fertilised the moment pollen lands on its stigma

questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Pollination is fertilisation. In fact Pollination is delivery: the male gamete must still fuse with the ovule for fertilisation. Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma; fertilisation is the later fusion inside the ovule.
questions.prompt: Which statement about pollination and fertilisation is correct?

choices.text: Pollination - the male gamete fuses with the ovule
Pollination - pollen is transferred from anther to stigma
Fertilisation - seeds are scattered from the parent

questions.explanation: Pollination is transfer between flowers; fertilisation is fusion inside the ovule. Scattering seeds is dispersal, a later step.
questions.prompt: Which pairing of event and meaning is correct?

questions.answer: Pollination has happened because the pollen was transferred to the stigma. Fertilisation has not happened because the male gamete never fused with the ovule.
questions.explanation: Landing completes delivery. Without the tube delivering the male nucleus to the ovule there is no fusion, so no fertilisation and no seed.
questions.prompt: A pollen grain lands on a stigma but its tube never reaches the ovule. State which event has happened and which has not, and why.

questions.answer: The pollen tube grows down the style and carries the male nucleus to the ovule so it can fuse with it.
questions.explanation: The tube is the bridge between delivery and fusion: it forms after pollination and makes fertilisation possible.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain the job of the pollen tube.

choices.text: Wind, water, animals and exploding pods

questions.explanation: Scene 3 shows wind lifting seeds, water carrying them, animals dropping them, and pods exploding to scatter them.
questions.prompt: Which list gives four ways seeds are dispersed in scene 3?
